ready.note: set in app.js armNext() after the first painted frame. The fonts clause is load-bearing: each frame opens a cold page, and a capture taken before the serif arrives rasterises every label in the fallback font — globe-default moved 1.016% on 2026-08-06 and the diff was nothing but label halos and reflowed voyage lists.

frames.name: descent
frames.note: The near field at 700 m: displaced water, the near/far seam and the horizon, off the Bristol Channel. ⚠ ITS NOTE USED TO CLAIM "the Great Western at true scale" AND NO HULL HAS EVER BEEN IN IT — checked pixelwise against the 2026-08-03 baseline on 2026-08-04: zero hull-dark pixels in either. The descent path does call psgFleet, so a hull within 182 km should draw; it does not, and that is an open bug rather than a framing accident. Until it is fixed this frame watches WATER, and nothing here defends the near-field fleet.

frames.name: descent-high
frames.note: Nine kilometres: just ABOVE the handover, so the token side of the seam is watched too. A frame on only one side of a boundary cannot see the boundary move. ⚠ Do not re-point this one northward — 51.1N 3.87W is over Exmoor and the frame comes back a near-black picture of unlit ground.

frames.name: descent-coast
frames.note: The near-field GROUND: the Strait of Gibraltar at 260 m, looking south at the Moroccan coast. The globe sphere is 192x128 — a 209 km facet — so at this eye height the backdrop is a flat plate with a polygon edge for a horizon and can never show a coast. This frame watches the displaced land patch that can.

frames.name: aboard
frames.note: ABOARD: the close-up, entered the way a viewer enters it — by naming a ship. This view is what the project is most often asked about and it had no baseline at all, for the plain reason that no URL could ask for it. Watches the true-scale hull, the near-field water it floats in, her wake, and the join between that water and the globe behind it.

frames.name: aboard-off
frames.note: ABOARD, a different era and hull: the container ship on the Asia-Europe run. Two frames rather than one because the close-up has to hold for a 400 m motor ship and a 72 m paddle steamer, and a single frame cannot see that.

frames.name: map-floor
frames.note: THE MAP AT ITS LOWEST — 300 km over the Serra do Mar, with Sousa's fleet closing the Brazilian coast for São Vicente. 300 km is where the token exaggeration peaks and therefore where the wheel now stops: below it the ramp unwinds the token toward true scale and the ship SHRANK, from 65 km long at 35.6% of the frame to 100 m at 2%. Watches the ship-to-coast proportion, which is the thing being asserted, and the water at that height. ⚠ Re-pointed r54: it framed the treasure fleet off Cape St Vincent until phases became identity-keyed (a hash of the voyage name, so data insertions stop moving unrelated ships) and the flota's own phase left her mid-Atlantic. Chosen the aboard-coast way — every era-4 ship's frozen position computed, the one against a coast taken.

frames.name: aboard-coast
frames.note: ABOARD, CLOSE INSHORE — the Athenian armada five kilometres off the Peloponnese, with land 121 m high and the sun 65 degrees up. August reported seeing NO LAND from the close-up while the map showed the ship hugging a coast, and no frame watched it: `aboard` and `aboard-off` both happen to sit in open water, and the first attempt at this frame put the guano clipper a thousand kilometres off Chile. Chosen by sweeping every ship in every era at the frozen instant for the one nearest to lit land, rather than by guessing.

frames.name: sea-magnified
frames.note: OPEN WATER AT 10 km — magnified far past the scale the sea shader was tuned for, which is the band between the near-field handover at 8 km and the old 12 km map floor. August photographed a regular lattice of pale dashes here and no frame watched it: every other water frame is either at globe zoom or in the near field. The cause was foam laid along the crests of a FOUR-component Gerstner sum — four sinusoids are visibly periodic once resolved, and white on their crests draws that periodicity. Measured by FFT: one component at 33 px, peak-to-mean 395, now 139.

frames.name: ship-preussen
frames.note: riveted 1902 steel windjammer — era-keyed dress: red-brown bottom, no cove line

frames.name: ship-steamer

frames.name: ship-dreadnought

frames.name: aboard-carrier
frames.note: ABOARD, THE CARRIER — the strike group on deployment. Added round 35 with the paint rebuild: she read as a black cutout in both views (deck 0x23272b, island 0x2b3036, topside #4e545b — soot albedos tuned to rigs). Watches the measured scheme — FS 26270 haze-grey verticals, weathered non-skid deck — and the deck markings, deck park and island against the reference relative pattern: island brightest, deck ~0.9×, shell 0.2–0.6×.

frames.name: aboard-cable
frames.note: ABOARD, THE LEVIATHAN — Great Eastern laying the Atlantic cable. Added round 40 with the paddle-box rebuild: from sea level the box must read as a closed drum standing on its sponson, fan face outboard, the open lower wheel entering the water beneath it.

frames.name: aboard-titanic
frames.note: ABOARD, THE LINER — Titanic on her maiden-voyage track. Added round 34 with the era profile rebuild: black shell to B deck with the white house above, forecastle/poop breaks, 9.46° raked buff funnels and masts whose trucks stand 62.5 m over the load line. The Sea view is where the r32 era-dress and this structure meet; no baseline watched a liner here before.

frames.name: aboard-yamato
frames.note: ABOARD, THE BATTLESHIP — Yamato on the Ten-ichi-go sortie. Added round 36 with her second detail pass: the 1941 close-in fit (eight shielded 25 mm triples on bandstands), searchlight platforms winged off the pagoda, stowage hatches on the quarterdeck and two floatplanes aft — one riding the port catapult. Watches the crowded amidships silhouette the record describes.

frames.name: aboard-preussen
frames.note: the doubled rig from on deck — 30 square sails, staysails, jibs and the spanker, round 44

frames.name: ship-wyoming
frames.note: the six-masted schooner — gaff quads, topsails, five headsails on the spike bowsprit, deckhouses (round 42)

frames.name: aboard-wyoming
frames.note: Wyoming at sea in the coal trade, close-up — the rig from the water (round 42)

frames.name: ship-treasure
frames.note: the junk grammar complete (round 46) — fanned battened lugs to steep yards, sheet crowfeet, bulkhead transoms both ends, the slung median rudder below the bottom, the tiered aft castle

frames.name: aboard-treasure
frames.note: ABOARD, THE TREASURE FLEET — Zheng He outbound, round 46. Watches the five fans drawing at sea, the castle and the blunt ends from the water. ⚠ e must be 4: the voyage lives in Ocean Crossing 1400–1800, and asking for it in era 3 leaves the app waiting forever and __FRAME_READY never fires.

frames.name: ship-clipper
frames.note: the record's full-rigger (round 51) — five yards to a mast with royals atop, four jibs on taut stays, six staysails, the spanker, two white deckhouses and the open wheel aft; rig scale anchored to RMG's 47 m main truck

frames.name: aboard-clipper
frames.note: ABOARD, THE WOOL RUN — the clipper running home, round 51. ⚠ e must be 5: woolrun is 1887 and lives in 1800–1900; a wrong era hangs the app before first paint (the treasure-fleet lesson).

frames.name: shipwright-ahead
frames.note: the standing aback guard: bow-on via #b=0, canvas must stand FORWARD of the masts. All square sails share makeSail, so this one bearing guards the fleet against the r52 mirror class regressing. Verified 2026-08-07 on five vessels from ahead and the quarter.

frames.name: shipwright-astern
frames.note: the standing stern guard: the 74 dead astern, close, aimed at the hull (#z/#l/#y, the r58 camera grammar). Every timber transom ship shares buildStern, so this one bearing watches the class: two tiers of lights, quarter galleries, taffrail. The r58 fault — furniture keyed to a stale u=0.985 plate, buried inside the u=1.0 skin — was invisible from every baseline bearing that existed before this frame.

frames.name: shipwright-furled
frames.note: the canvas STATE guard: the 74 from the port quarter, furled — every square roll, its gaskets and bunt, the hauled clews, and the whole yard built in the furled state behind her. One bearing watches the class; every rig type shares makeFurl.

frames.name: shipwright-hounds
frames.note: r64 standing guard on the masthead class: the 74's main lower masthead from the port quarter — cheeks under the trestletree pair, the doubling between them, wooldings with their wooden hoops down the made mast. Guards item 9's whole class (wooldings/iron hoops by S.year, cheeks per doubled masthead).

frames.name: shipwright-corbis
frames.note: r67 standing guard: masthead furniture per the evidence — the corbita's bare head (no top before 1100) with the corbis, the basket that named her (Festus). Watches the dated-top class and the corbis class.

frames.name: ship-azzam
frames.note: the 2013 Lürssen yacht with her plate-derived mast/stack/radome cluster (r73) — every height derived from the delivery photograph, labelled so

frames.name: ship-endurance
frames.note: the one hull that had no frame was the one that crashed when opened (round 101) — unphotographed corners hide faults by construction

frames.name: action-salamis
frames.note: the galley action: Salamis at the crush, 130 m, both fleets triremes under bare spars — guards the data-driven campaign class (fleets/formation/powder/year from the record)

frames.name: board-salamis
frames.note: the globe CAMPAIGN BOARD, addressable at last (r82) — Salamis day 0 at the record's own cam (450 km over the Saronic Gulf), one token per fleet per the fits-test, tracks, wind streaks and the campaign bar. The board was dead for nine days (c66c703) because no frame could name it; this one guards the class the audit's step-every-campaign rule only smoke-tests.

frames.name: action-gravelines
frames.note: GRAVELINES from the water, day 9 at 110 m — the only close action of the Armada campaign, with the r84 DEM coast wearing the r85 data-keyed polder palette (pasture green, dune-sand waterline, Dunkirk dunes as fogged headlands E). Guards the shore-palette class: a coast wearing another climate's colours moves this frame.

frames.name: action-lepanto
frames.note: Lepanto, early afternoon 7 October 1571 — the north flank: Barbarigo's wing and Scirocco's locked at 200 m under the Scropha rise, the delta spit at the waterline. Watches the lepanto.png shore render, the grounding rule, the third-fleet (side:0) staging and the authored day heading (hd).

frames.name: wake-plan
frames.note: THE WAKE FROM ABOVE — the container ship at 20 kn, near-plan through the r111 follow-camera grammar (fb/fd/fz). The wake shipped wrong twice (r44 steps, r111 ladder-and-blob) because every addressable camera was deck-level and nearly edge-on: no frame could see the Kelvin pattern at all. Watches the wedge springing from the stem, the curved transverse crests (phase from the dispersion relation, 1.00 on the track to 1.53 at the cusp), the feathered arms, the bow horseshoe with dark water ahead of her, and the turbulent band from the stern.

frames.name: ship-ever-given
frames.note: THE TWIN-ISLAND SHIP — added round 113 with her rebuild from the PMA casualty report. No frame watched her before, which is how a bridge drawn 190 m from its recorded station survived 66 rounds. Watches: the accommodation tower in the fore third (mast at u 0.366, the loading computer's own figure), the dark-green engine casing and stack at u 0.845, EVERGREEN on the shell, EVER GIVEN / PANAMA on the transom, the 17.2 m freeboard wall under a ten-tier stow.

frames.name: sea-ever-given
frames.note: THE TWIN-ISLAND SHIP AT SEA — round 113 rebuilt her from the PMA casualty report but only the Shipwright watched her; this frame stands 800 m off her port beam at sea level on the westbound Arabian Sea leg (course 283°, 22.8 kn). Watches: the accommodation tower a third from the bow and the dark-green casing aft among the stacks (the twin-island layout), EVERGREEN on the shell reading correctly on the port side, the 17.2 m freeboard wall with the boot-top at the water, the bow wave and the near arm of her wake.

frames.name: passage-sahul
frames.note: THE FIRST CROSSING, IN ITS OWN DAYLIGHT - added r124. Era 0 at the era's own datum (the r123 fix this frame stands guard over); frozen t=374 puts local noon on the Timor Sea (subsolar lon = 0.006t rad). Camera pinned by fb/fd/fz so the frame watches the two open dugouts and their wakes, not standOffFor's land-height guess. No land in sight is CORRECT - the voyage card's own row says 70-90 km out of sight of land. The land row must stay unnamed at 60,000 BC (r124 gazetteer existence gate).

frames.name: sea-dugout-floor
frames.note: THE OPEN HULL'S FLOOR, WATCHED - added r127. 55 deg down at 30 m over the followed Sahul dugout: the one angle that sees past the rim to the hollowed floor and the stowed gear (spare paddles, bailer) the record attests. Every other committed frame takes the floor on faith - the r114 one-view-blindness class. Same frozen noon as passage-sahul.
